acceptance_criteria.criterion: candidate admission rejects writer/committer mismatch before remote push and reports the exact mismatched provenance claim
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Header-level writer/committer mismatch rejection before push already exists on the trusted base (scripts/hunter_writer_provenance.py evaluate_commit/evaluate_range, run by .githooks/pre-push) and is unchanged here. This PR establishes, on the trusted default branch and outside the candidate it will judge, the exact root-of-trust data the key-level half needs: signing_key_bindings binds claude -> SHA256:32dP45eSMmVSt/G/CGvcxl/P+MO3Nwj9xeTh/GSA2wc and fafa33 -> SHA256:Yee9tbonym7Jvs2UbjpudVIRkv3aF1tcFlK240pXuBo, each with recorded trusted evidence, require_key_bound_to_resolved_writer=true, and explicit fail-closed and unsigned-commit semantics. tests/test_signing_key_binding_bootstrap.py pins the exact bindings (any self-binding, replacement or extra key fails), requires one key set per bound login with full SHA-256 fingerprints and no key shared between writers, and requires evidence for each key.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: commit attribution to an implementation agent can coexist with the authorization-bound writer identity without weakening auditability
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Attribution remains trailer-only (attribution_semantics unchanged); identity is still read only from author/committer headers. The new bindings give each writer exactly its own key (claude's key is not bound to fafa33 and vice versa; test_every_bound_writer_has_exactly_its_own_explicit_key), so agent attribution coexists with the bound writer identity, and auditability is strengthened because a commit's real signing key can be tied to the writer it claims.

defect_families.evidence: No authorization path or replayable token is introduced; the change is static policy data. A binding cannot be replayed onto another writer because each fingerprint is bound to exactly one login, and the test forbids sharing a key between writers.

History-forgery resistance: bindings are evidenced by trusted-main %GK fingerprints and the GitHub-registered owner key, not by candidate-supplied claims. The exact-binding test makes any later edit to the root-of-trust data a deliberate, reviewed test change.
